events.title: Catrìona's request to Silas Crewe
events.body: Catrìona nic Eachainn, crew-leader of the seventh shift at Baile thais, asks the agent Silas Crewe to close the third and fourth galleries, where the Green Death struck worst, until the surgeon rules on the dust. Crewe answers that the yield must not fall on a physician's guess, and says only that he will write it up.

events.title: Sìneag searches the old rolls for a law of rest
events.body: Asked by Catrìona nic Eachainn whether any old law binds a hill's rest, the custodian Sìneag of Baile thais searches her rolls and finds none: Lagh an Loscaidh Bhig governs the coal burned, not the coal cut, and no custodian before this age had needed to write a law about men sickening below ground.

events.title: The shrine women keep the green acre through the stoppage
events.body: Through the eleven days no coal left Baile thais, the shrine women go on leaving dishes of meal on the mounds of the green acre where the Green Death's dead were laid, finding a little to spare each day though A' Chompanaidh's store stood barer by the day beside them.

events.title: Beathag Ruadh asks Catrìona to end the stand
events.body: On the tenth night of the stoppage, her bread gone and five children to feed, Beathag Ruadh asks Catrìona nic Eachainn, plainly and without reproach, whether the crews should go back below rather than starve for galleries that would go on being worked regardless. Catrìona has no answer, and sits with her by the fire till morning.

events.title: Dòmhnall Maor signs the granary order
events.body: Within the month of the strike's end, Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill Maor, Steward at Muileann chrom, sets his mark to the order that forbids any camp household to keep more grain than a week's ration, the rest to be held under lock in A' Chompanaidh's new granary and drawn against a crew-leader's tally.

events.title: Sìneag's rolls note a granary built against a stoppage
events.body: The custodian Sìneag writes in her rolls that she has never before read of a granary raised to answer a stoppage rather than a harvest, and sets the words down as they stand, without further comment, for whoever should read the roll after her.

events.title: Catrìona walks east over the hills to Muileann chiar
events.body: With her savings spent and refused work at every Company pit, Catrìona nic Eachainn takes what she owns and walks east from Baile thais over the hills to Muileann chiar, three days on foot, the black spoil of the coal country giving way at last to the grey of the silver town.

events.title: Three priests will not stand for the blessing
events.body: Three of the younger priests of Òrd Mhacha stand apart at the back of the temple hall rather than take their places for the blessing of the coin. Beathag Ruadh lets it pass unremarked before the Residency's clerk, and tells Fearghas mac Mhuirich only that the order answers for the rite done rightly, not for the road a rightly blessed thing afterward walks.

events.title: Artair mac Iain seated after ten empty years
events.body: The Council of Custodians, unable to agree a head since Alasdair Liath's death, seats Artair mac Iain of the eastern shires as high custodian, six-and-fifty years old, in the hall where Tormod mac Ailein once signed the treaty. Fearghas mac Mhuirich says the order's blessing over him, both horses named.

events.title: The second cheapening cried at the market crosses
events.body: A Residency crier reads the second cheapening of the barter table at every market cross without a custodian's council having seen it beforehand. Word of it reaches Muileann chiar three days after Cathair dhearg, carried by a carter who had heard it cried at Baile Mòr fhionn.

events.title: Fearghas refuses to bless the second coin
events.body: Asked to bless the Administration's larger second coin as the first was blessed, Fearghas mac Mhuirich, now eldest of the order at Cathair dhearg since Beathag Ruadh's death, tells the order he will not say the words, holding that a rite for a wheel cannot answer a road that turns only one way. None of the order says the words in his place.

events.title: The Residency notes the order divided
events.body: Word of Fearghas mac Mhuirich's refusal reaches the Residency within the month. Tolley, near his own retiring, does not send for him; the Residency's letter-book records only that the order of Òrd Mhacha at the capital is divided on a religious nicety, and does not say what the nicety was.

events.title: Dòmhnall Maor dies at Muileann chrom
events.body: Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill Maor, overseer of the coal country five-and-twenty years and signer of the granary order that stood against Catrìona nic Eachainn's strike, dies at Muileann chrom in his sixty-seventh year. Word reaches Muileann chiar by carter, and the guild hall names him a hard man gone before a harder trade going on.

events.title: Fearghas leaves the capital's temple for Cnoc bheag
events.body: Fearghas mac Mhuirich walks north with eleven of the order who think as he does, to the sacred forest at Cnoc bheag. Griogair, eldest of those who stay at Cathair dhearg, walks with them as far as the north road and calls it two roads to the one rite rather than a falling-out.

events.title: The wrong son taken at Caol mhòr
events.body: A guessed name is matched to the wrong face at Caol mhòr's reading, and a son is marched a day's walk east before the error is found. The right man is fetched in his place; the officers' own tally and the town's roll never afterward agree by one head.

events.title: The concession's human farmers spared the Levy
events.body: In the northern concession the Levy falls on every Dia-thìreach household while the Administration's own leaseholders pay nothing, the officers' list giving the reason that the concession's tenants answer to the Administration's leave alone.

events.title: The Levy read at Cnoc thais
events.body: The Levy's officers read their list at Cnoc thais, and the mason Dùghall Clachair hears his own name and his whole crew's called for the pits. Two days into the eastward march they are turned out instead to the headland at Baile chrom, where the fifth and last coast beacon is begun.

events.title: The masons' camp above Baile chrom
events.body: Levy-taken crews from five villages are housed together in a turf-and-driftwood camp on the Baile chrom headland, above sixty masons and apprentices sharing one fire and one quarry, while their own villages' fields stand untilled for want of them.

events.title: A gale strips the beacon's scaffold
events.body: A two-day gale out of the north-west tears the scaffolding from the third course of the rising tower at Baile chrom. Dùghall Clachair climbs the bare walls alone in the wind to judge whether the stone has shifted; it has not.

events.title: Uisdean mac Lachlainn named keeper of Taigh-solais Baile chrom
events.body: Uisdean mac Lachlainn of the headland villages is named the beacon's first keeper, on the recommendation of the very masons who built it: Dùghall Clachair among them, who signed the letter along with two of his crew.
